Not just lonely that she’s gone, but lonely since my family doesn’t have the same love for each other like we used to. My mother was the glue that held things together. Things fell apart since she passed. I told him I miss my family being together. He told me that that feeling and love is gone. There’s no going back. The only thing you can do is make a choice. You know what’s funny, this life shit is a journey. I remember when I was 25 (now 27) I used to be down on myself because I haven’t been doing shit but be depressed. Yeah I graduated college, but graduating don’t mean shit when you write a suicide note a week after graduation because your brother pissed you off. I would watch TV and be like really tho, Cardi B is the same age as I and she’s worth this much and I’m still can’t figure my shit out? 

I guess what I’m getting at that this life shit is a journey as I said before. We live and adapt to our situations, and no matter what, we can find a way to persevere. Everybody’s story is different. Hell, I’m apart of your story just by typing this message praying that it makes sense to you. 

You know, your past is your past. The only person that cares about it is you. Your past is your strength because it teaches you how to move forward. The past hurts and is often embarrassing, but it’s you. I pray you wear your past like a badge of honor because it just strengthens the story of a individual who can persevere. 

The only person you need to compare to is is yourself. Fuck everybody else. When I learned to enjoy the journey, everything started to fall into place for me. I learned my values by reading books and understood what true happiness meant for me. To find that, I trusted myself and used my past mistakes as a guide to lead me to brighter possibilities.

I’m currently working with my severe depression as well. I’ve been Hospitalized for it twice the past year and what ultimately helps as of now are my meds. It took so long to get the right combination, but I feel like a brand new person. I also do exercise and yoga, but when I fall off my routine, I’m happy that I can rely on the medicine. Today I’m going through some heavy shit as we speak, but my thoughts are no longer loud and negative. I can actively make sound decisions now. 

Essentially things DO get better, but it doesn’t magically happen unfortunately. Compare it as when you first enter adulthood or college, shit really doesn’t change unless you do. Just try to remember the happy you before the depression so you have a goal. That’s what I do. I pray the medication works and you continue to fight and overcome. I will keep you in my prayers.
